open_points.subject: store.read_records relation call contract
open_points.text: "A call names the relation and passes the records its name mentions — a slot, a contract version, an implementation and a corpus digest, a flow, a flow version and a run, a run, an element, a flow version's node — or, for \"by status\", the status."
open_points.question: For each named relation, what is the exact required argument list and order, and what exact error is returned for extra/irrelevant-but-well-typed arguments?
options: Define one fixed argument schema per relation, with positional order and exact validation errors
Accept a looser argument bag and ignore unused arguments
open_points.default_guess: Define strict per-relation argument schemas and treat any extra argument as internal_error, matching the defect language.

open_points.subject: Refusal reason payload across operations
open_points.text: "refuses with one code of the closed set below and a bounded reason naming the first failing check in its rule's order."
open_points.question: Are refusal reasons free text, or a closed symbolic set per operation/check that callers/tests can rely on?
options: Free-text reason that merely mentions the check
Closed machine-stable reason identifiers per check
open_points.default_guess: Use stable symbolic reason identifiers (short strings) even if human-readable text is also included.

open_points.subject: MCP read_spooled_file request fields vs lookup identity
open_points.text: "its digest, size and media type only describe it — an identity naming no SpooledFile is `unknown_reference`"
open_points.question: If caller-supplied digest/size/media_type do not match the stored SpooledFile named by identity, should the call fail or ignore those descriptive fields?
options: Ignore descriptive mismatches and use only lookup identity fields
Validate descriptive fields against stored record and refuse on mismatch
open_points.default_guess: Ignore descriptive fields for lookup and do not fail on mismatch, because text says they only describe.

open_points.subject: list_records filter semantics for node execution aliases
open_points.text: "node executions (the trace) | `run_id`, `executed_implementation`, `executed_binding` — two names for M23's one `executed` field, by the kind of record it names"
open_points.question: When filtering by `executed_implementation` or `executed_binding`, is kind-constrained matching mandatory even if raw identifiers could collide in string form?
options: Alias implies strict kind + identifier match
Alias is only a field name alias and matches by raw identifier equality
open_points.default_guess: Require strict kind-constrained matching (implementation records only for `executed_implementation`, binding records only for `executed_binding`).

open_points.subject: record_run_progress payload cardinality
open_points.text: "`record_run_progress` | `runs` | NodeExecutions M23 written together ...; then the run's status, outputs, WaitingPoints M20, `ended_at`, `cancelled_by`"
open_points.question: Must `record_run_progress` include at least one new NodeExecution, or may it legally write only derived run fields (status/waiting/output changes) with zero new executions?
options: Require at least one NodeExecution in every record_run_progress call
Allow zero-execution progress updates when only derived run fields change
open_points.default_guess: Allow zero-execution progress updates, since run derivation may change after prior writes by other changes.
